channel.title: Signet Artists | Blog
channel.description: We’re Signet Artists in Denver, and we write now and then about live music for private events, including how to plan it, what it costs and the music itself.

item.title: How to choose music for an event
item.description: We start with who is coming and what the night is for, then check the space and the schedule. Genre comes last. How we match a crowd to an act.

item.title: Hispanic Heritage Month ideas for the office: a mariachi band
item.description: Hispanic Heritage Month runs September 15 to October 15. A mariachi band and a taco truck during the workday: when it fits and what to pair it with.

item.title: What music is Colorado known for?
item.description: Colorado is known for John Denver, bluegrass and jam bands. Here is what Denver, Boulder, Colorado Springs and the ski towns sound like now.

item.title: What does Denver sound like?
item.description: Denver sounds like neo-soul with a mountain sensibility, with funk, jazz and a scene of roots songwriters. Here is where to hear it and who plays it.

item.title: How to make a corporate event sound like Colorado
item.description: Decide whether the music is the event or the background, then pick by city. Local music for corporate events in Denver, Boulder and Colorado Springs.

item.title: Chantil Dukart joins Signet Artists
item.description: Denver jazz pianist and singer Chantil Dukart joins Signet Artists. Book her solo at the piano, as a duo, with her trio or with a five-piece band in Colorado.

item.title: Quadrasonic brings Signet Artists to Vail
item.description: Vail Valley rock band Quadrasonic joins Signet Artists. Book a band that lives in Vail for weddings in Vail and Beaver Creek, retreats and parties.

item.title: Roma Ransom joins Signet Artists
item.description: Roma Ransom, a violin and guitar duo from Colorado Springs playing Romanian and Eastern European folk, old-time ballads and swing, joins Signet Artists.

item.title: Emily Barnes joins Signet Artists
item.description: Award-winning folk singer-songwriter Emily Barnes joins Signet Artists. Book her solo, as a duo with guitar or fiddle, or as a trio in Colorado.

item.title: Chelsey Webb joins Signet Artists
item.description: Denver country singer Chelsey Webb, 2025 Female Entertainer of the Year, joins Signet Artists. Book her as a duo or with her five or six-piece band.

item.title: Why guests can't hear the toast
item.description: Why wedding toasts and event speeches get lost: the microphone held too low, the squeal, and music left up under the voice. What to ask your band and venue so every table hears every word.

item.title: Why dinner gets louder as the night goes on
item.description: Why an event gets louder on its own: past about 57 decibels guests raise their voices and the whole space climbs. What loud music does to drinking, ordering, taste and older guests, and the two-level plan that keeps dinner talkable.

item.title: What your venue does to the sound
item.description: Why live music sounds harsh in a glass venue and muddy in a carpeted one, what echo does to speeches, a clap test any planner can do, and why where the speakers point matters more than how big they are.

item.title: Meghan Clarisse joins Signet Artists
item.description: Award-winning Denver country and Americana singer-songwriter Meghan Clarisse joins Signet Artists. Book her solo, as a duo or with her five-piece band.

item.title: How much sound system does an event need?
item.description: What wattage actually buys (doubling it adds three decibels), why headroom and speaker placement matter more, and why the outlet behind the band must be on its own circuit, away from the coffee urn.

item.title: Why does music bring back memories?
item.description: Why does music bring back memories? Here's what studies found about memory, nostalgia and 'our song', and how you can use it at an anniversary party.

item.title: Why do restaurants have live music?
item.description: Why do restaurants have live music? Here's what studies found about how long guests stay, what they spend and how loud the music should be.

item.title: Why do people sing along?
item.description: Wondering why people sing along at concerts and parties? We looked at a study of 1,054 songs and at whether singing together brings people closer.

item.title: Why do people play music at funerals?
item.description: Why is music part of a funeral? Here's what studies say about how families choose the song, what people often pick, and whether it has to be a hymn.

item.title: Why do dementia patients remember music?
item.description: Why do people with dementia often remember old songs? Here's what a song can bring back, which songs last, and what researchers found music can't do for memory.
